newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK YIELD CURVE, BONDS HOLD, ECU/DRS RANGES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK YIELD CURVE, BONDS HOLD, ECU/DRS RANGES.

text.p: Greek bonds and FRNs were steady in a nervous market, short-dated depos and forex forwards were holding Friday's high levels hovering around 11.90 percent and ecu/drachma was rangebound, dealers said.

"Bonds and FRNs are little changed but the market is still nervous," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "High interbank rates, the offspring of tighter liquidity conditions, have many investors wary."

The market will be awaiting to hear the amount of 14-day funds that the central bank will tender on Wednesday. Bank of Greece surprised the market in last week's depo tender by soaking about 50 billion drachmas more than expiries at 11.90 percent.

The dealer said tax-free FRNs due 2003 got a boost from the finance ministry's announcement on Friday that it would slash spreads over the benchmark 12-month T-bill by 50 basis points to 0.80 percent effective June 9.
"The spread cut helped tax-free FRNs due 2003," the dealer said. "These FRNs were trading at a discount margin of 80/85 basis points before the announcement to fall back to 65/70."
Depos and forex forwards were fluctuating narrowly in early dealings with shorts hovering around 11.90 percent, dealers said.
"Liquidity-driven shorts are holding high Friday levels," traders said. "The market eyes Wednesday's depo tender to gauge the central bank's stance," a dealer at a private bank said.
The mark was quoted at 159.00/10 from Friday's 158.785 fix, the dollar at 274.11/21 drachmas from 275.560 and the ecu at 309.90/00 from 309.830 drachmas.
Ecu/drachma opened around 310 to recede later to 309.80/85 on ecu selling for drachmas by domestic players beforing driven up again to 310, forex dealers said.
"The forex market is calm and spot ecu/drachma is rangebound with its downside risk limited due to the higher interest rates," a forex dealer at a foreign bank said.
